items.requirement: State the research question: how can a dataset collected by a moving robot capture real-world pedestrian–robot interactions and support pedestrian perception and motion prediction for social navigation?
items.quote:
reflects
the interactive behaviors between pedestrians and a mobile robot in the real world

items.requirement: Describe collection by a manually operated robot in crowded indoor and outdoor locations in Seoul, with two 3D LiDARs and five cameras synchronized by a pulse-per-second trigger and providing 360-degree camera coverage.
items.quote: we employed a pulse per second (PPS) signal generator to trigger two 3D LiDARs and five cameras.

items.requirement: Report the dataset scale of 60 scenes, 60K images, and 12K point-cloud frames, with 20-second sequences sampled at 10 Hz. Identify the 2D and 3D box annotations, object IDs, and multilayer semantic maps.
items.quote: Our entire dataset comprises 60 scenes, totaling 60K images and 12K point cloud frames.

items.requirement: Explain that pedestrian trajectories compensate for robot ego-motion and that training, validation, and test subsets contain different scenes.
items.quote:
We split
the dataset so that each subset encompasses different scenes.

items.requirement: Report that SiT has more trajectory instances meeting both interaction criteria than Waymo Open, Argoverse 2, and nuScenes. Define the criteria as occupying the same semantic space and being within 2 meters of the robot or ego vehicle.
items.quote:
the SiT dataset exhibits a significantly higher number of
instances that satisfy these two conditions compared to the other three autonomous driving datasets.

items.requirement: Identify the 3D detection baselines FCOS3D, PointPillars, CenterPoint, and TransFusion, and the tracking baselines AB3DMOT with PointPillars or CenterPoint detections and the CenterPoint tracker. Specify that detection mAP averages center-distance AP at 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 meters, and that tracking uses sAMOTA, AMOTA, AMOTP, MOTA, MOTP, and identity switches.
items.quote:
we adopt AP based on the distance metric using the thresholds of
0.25, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0m.

items.requirement: Describe the trajectory forecasting protocol using 2 seconds of history and 7 seconds of future motion, with minimum ADE and FDE over 5 and 20 candidates. Name Social-LSTM, Y-Net, and NSP-SFM, and report that semantic maps reduced displacement errors for Y-Net and NSP-SFM in the reported comparisons.
items.quote:
we confirm the benefit of utilizing scene contexts
for trajectory prediction.

items.requirement: Describe the end-to-end benchmark as predicting future 3D boxes and associated trajectories from raw sensor data over 7 seconds. Identify Fast and Furious and the two FutureDet variants, and distinguish standard mAP, forecasting mAP, ADE at five candidates, and FDE at five candidates in the reported comparison.
items.quote:
the models take raw
sensor data as input and generate future 3D bounding boxes

items.requirement: State the authors’ dataset-scale limitation: time constraints prevented collection at the scale of hundreds of thousands of frames.
items.quote:
we were unable to scale the size of the dataset up to hundreds
of thousands of frames due to time constraints.
